questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests understanding of Helm templating and basic policy checks in CI for secure defaults, plus ability to craft a simple gate that a junior engineer can implement.

## Key Concepts

- Helm templating and values.yaml
- YAML validation with yq
- Kubernetes securityContext basics
- Image tag policy and registry scoping
- CI gate design and test manifests

## Code Example

```yaml
# .github/workflows/helm-gate.yml
name: Helm gate
on: push
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: azure/setup-helm@v1
      - name: Render charts
        run: helm template mychart charts/mychart > /tmp/rendered.yaml
      - name: Validate images
        run: |
          if ! yq e '.items[].spec.template.spec.containers[].image' /tmp/rendered.yaml | grep -q registry.example.com/secure/; then echo image origin invalid; exit 1; fi
```

```yaml
# failing Deployment manifest
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myservice
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: registry.example.com/secure/myservice:latest
          # missing securityContext and resources
```

```yaml
# passing Deployment manifest
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myservice
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: registry.example.com/secure/myservice:v1.2.3
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 1000
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 128Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 200m
              memory: 256Mi
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you extend to multi-container pods?
- How would you adapt for multiple charts in a single repo?

## Why This Is Asked

Deprecations pose production risk in multi-tenant clusters. This question probes practical policy design across CI and runtime using Gatekeeper and Kyverno, plus concrete manifests and validation strategy.

## Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Kyverno admission policies
- Kubernetes API deprecations and upgrade paths
- CI validation with kubeconform/kubeval
- Runtime admission controls and auditability

## Code Example

```yaml
# Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate (simplified)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sdeprecatedapi
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sDeprecatedAPI
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8sdeprecatedapi
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        deprecated := ["apps/v1beta1", "networking.k8s.io/v1beta1"]
        api := input.review.object.apiVersion
        api == deprecated[_]
        msg := sprintf("deprecated apiVersion used: %v", [api])
      }
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (deprecated API)
apiVersion: apps/v1beta1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: old-deploy
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/old:1
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (stable API)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: new-deploy
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/new:1
```

- How would you extend to cover CRDs and future API regressions?
- How would you surface violations to developers and enforce remediation in PRs?

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a practical, policy-driven CI/CD gate for hybrid cloud/edge Kubernetes, focusing on provenance, reproducibility, and runtime enforcement. It mixes static checks in CI with runtime admission controls, using cosign, SBOMs, and a central provenance store.

Key Concepts

- Cosign verification with in-repo public key
- SBOM generation/verification for artifacts
- ProvenanceDigest tied to a central store and manifest cross-check
- Kyverno policy for runtime rejection of unsigned/mismatched provenance
- Minimal GitHub Actions workflow and OPA policy demonstrating end-to-end flow

Code Example

```javascript
name: ci-gate
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: verify cosign
        run: cosign verify -key cosign.pub image:tag
      - name: verify SBOM
        run: bash -lc 'cat sbom.json | jq .'
      - name: provenance check
        run: bash -lc 'grep -q provenanceDigest <manifest.yaml && echo ok'
```

Follow-up Questions

- How would you rotate cosign keys with zero-downtime for edge clusters?
- How would you test this gate against evolving provenance schemas and multi-tenant RBAC?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design runtime security controls that span CI, policy engines, and multi cloud networking, ensuring outbound traffic is strictly controlled and auditable.

## Key Concepts

- Policy-as-code (Gatekeeper/OPA)
- Egress gateway design and TLS origination
- Outbound allowlist management
- CI validation for policy enforcement
- Cross-cloud consistency and testing

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate for Gatekeeper enforcing egress gateway annotation
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8segressgateway
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sEgressPolicy
  targets:
  - target: obj  # pseudo example for clarity
    rego: |
      package k8segress
      default deny = true
      deny[msg] = msg {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        not input.review.object.metadata.annotations["egress.gateway/enforced"] == "true"
        msg := "Pod must set egress.gateway/enforced=true to route via central gateway"
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint demonstrating allowlist usage (illustrative)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sEgressPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-egress-gateway
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        kinds: ["Pod"]
  parameters:
    allowlist: ["app.allowed.example.com"]
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (no egress annotation or disallowed destination)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: bad-egress-pod
  annotations:
    # missing or false
    egress.gateway/enforced: "false"
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:latest
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (annotation set and allowlisted destination)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: good-egress-pod
  annotations:
    egress.gateway/enforced: "true"
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:1.23.4
```

## Local and CI Validation

- Local: run gatekeeper locally to test ConstraintTemplate/Constraint; simulate Pod admission with k8s manifest.
- CI: run a workflow that lints manifests, validates policy via a test cluster or KinD, and fails on noncompliant manifests.

## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates real-world expertise in supply chain security by testing the ability to tie SBOMs to runtime admission policies. It aligns with vendor-agnostic security frameworks (SLSA, SBOM) and modern GitOps deployment patterns where provenance verification is critical.

## Key Concepts

- **CycloneDX SBOMs**: Standardized software bills of materials that document container contents
- **Image digests**: SHA256 references ensuring immutable image pinning
- **Kyverno admission control**: Policy engine validating deployments at Kubernetes admission time
- **Helm chart provenance**: Ensuring charts reference verified, SBOM-backed images

## Proposed Solution

### GitHub Actions Workflow: Generate and Publish SBOMs

```yaml
name: SBOM Pipeline
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  build-and-sbom:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - uses: anchore/sbom-action@v0
        with:
          format: cyclonedx-json
          image: ${{ github.repository }}
          output-file: sbom.json
      - run: |
          echo "${{ steps.sbom.outputs.sbom-json }}" | ghcr.io/your-org/sbom-store:latest 
            --image=${{ github.repository }}@${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}
```

### Kyverno Policy: Enforce SBOM Presence at Admission

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-image-sbom
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  background: true
  rules:
  - name: validate-sbom-present
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
        - Deployment
        - StatefulSet
        - DaemonSet
    preconditions:
      any:
      - key: "{{ request.operation }}"
        operator: In
        value: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
    validate:
      message: "All container images must have an associated CycloneDX SBOM"
      foreach:
      - list: "{{ request.object.spec.template.spec.containers[] }}"
        deny:
          conditions:
          - key: "{{ element.image }}"
            operator: NotEqual
            value: ""
          - key: "{{ lookup('sbom.verify', '{{ element.image }}', 'cyclonedx') }}"
            operator: NotEqual
            value: "valid"
```

### Failing Manifest (No SBOM)

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: vulnerable-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: vulnerable-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: vulnerable-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:1.25
```

**Expected Result**: Deployment blocked with error: "All container images must have an associated CycloneDX SBOM"

### Passing Manifest (SBOM Verified)

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: verified-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: verified-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: verified-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: ghcr.io/your-org/app@sha256:a1b2c3d4e5f6...
        annotations:
          sbom.cyclonedx: "ghcr.io/your-org/app/sbom/a1b2c3d4e5f6"
```

**Expected Result**: Deployment allowed

## Testing Steps

1. **Apply Kyverno policy**: `kubectl apply -f kyverno-policy.yaml`
2. **Test failing manifest**: `kubectl apply -f deployment-no-sbom.yaml` — should be rejected
3. **Test passing manifest**: `kubectl apply -f deployment-with-sbom.yaml` — should be admitted
4. **Verify SBOM storage**: Confirm SBOMs are queryable via your SBOM service endpoint
5. **Audit logs**: Check Kyverno policy reports for enforcement details

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked

This question evaluates a candidate's ability to design production-grade policy gates that enforce artifact provenance and data lineage—critical concerns in multi-cloud ML deployments where governance and compliance are paramount. The question tests practical experience with cryptographic attestation, policy-as-code frameworks, and CI/CD pipeline design.

## Sample OPA Policy

```rego
package data.provenance

default allow = false

allow {
    input.review.kind == "Deployment"
    some i
    input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers[i].image
    startswith(image, input.config.trusted_registry)
    verify_signature(image)
    tenant_allowed(input.review.namespace)
    lineage_tag_valid(image)
}

verify_signature(image) {
    not missing_signature(image)
    crypto.verify(input.artifacts[image].sig, input.artifacts[image].digest, input.config.public_key)
}

missing_signature(image) {
    not input.artifacts[image]
}

tenant_allowed(ns) {
    input.config.tenant_allowlist[ns]
}

lineage_tag_valid(image) {
    tag := input.artifacts[image].lineage_tag
    input.catalog.tags[tag]
}
```

## Sample Kyverno Policy

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: ml-artifact-provenance
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
  - name: validate-signed-artifact
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
    preconditions:
      any:
      - key: '{{ request.namespace }}'
        operator: In
        value: '{{ tenantAllowlist }}'
    validate:
      message: "Artifact must be signed and from trusted registry"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - image: '{{ trustedRegistry }}@*'
      foreach:
      - list: "{{ request.object.spec.template.spec.containers[] }}"
        preconditions:
          all:
          - key: "{{ element.image }}"
            operator: NotIn
            value: [""]
        context:
        - name: artifactData
          apiCall:
            urlPath: "/artifacts/{{ element.image | split("@")[1] }}"
        - name: signatureValid
          apiCall:
            urlPath: "/verify/{{ artifactData.digest }}"
            statement: "$.signature.valid == true"
```

## Failing Manifest Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: model-inference
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: inference
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: inference
        image: untrusted-registry.com/models:v1.0  # ❌ Not in trusted registry
        env:
        - name: ARTIFACT_DIGEST
          value: "sha256:abc123"
        - name: LINEAGE_TAG
          value: "raw-data-v2"  # ❌ Tag not in data catalog
```

**Failure Reasons:**
1. Image not from trusted registry
2. Lineage tag `raw-data-v2` not registered in data catalog
3. Missing cryptographic signature
4. Tenant `tenant-a` not in allowlist

## Passing Manifest Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: model-inference
  namespace: tenant-a
  annotations:
    artifact.provenance/digest: "sha256:def456"
    artifact.provenance/signature: "LS0tLS1..."
    artifact.provenance/tenant: "tenant-a"
    artifact.provenance/lineage: "processed-features-v1"
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: inference
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: inference
        image: trusted-registry.com/tenant-a/models:v2.1@sha256:def456  # ✓ Trusted registry
        env:
        - name: ARTIFACT_DIGEST
          value: "sha256:def456"
        - name: LINEAGE_TAG
          value: "processed-features-v1"  # ✓ Tag exists in catalog
```

## CI Verification Steps

1. **Extract artifact reference** from deployment manifest
2. **Fetch artifact metadata** from trusted registry API
3. **Validate cryptographic signature** against registry's public key
4. **Verify tenant allowlist** — confirm namespace exists in per-tenant policy
5. **Check data catalog** — confirm lineage tag is registered and active
6. **Attest result** — write provenance record to audit log with timestamp and CI run ID
7. **Block or permit** pipeline execution based on policy evaluation

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8snetworkidentity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sNetworkIdentityConstraint
  targets:
  - target: Kubernetes
    rego: |
      package k8snetworkidentity
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind == "Deployment"
        not has_ns_deny_ingress(input)
        msg := "Deployment namespace must have a deny-ingress NetworkPolicy and allow only whitelisted sources."
      }
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (no deny ingress and automount enabled)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example-fail
  namespace: dev
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: example-fail
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: example-fail
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:alpine
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (deny ingress, trusted SA, automount disabled)
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: app-sa
  namespace: dev
  annotations:
    trusted.example.io: "true"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: example-pass
  namespace: dev
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: example-pass
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: example-pass
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: app-sa
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:alpine
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
```

```yaml
# Minimal NetworkPolicy (deny ingress by default, allow from trusted namespace)
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-ingress
  namespace: dev
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          env: trusted
```

## CI Verification Steps
- Gatekeeper audit run in CI to ensure constraints are evaluated.
- kubectl apply --dry-run=client -f failing.yaml should trigger policy violations.
- kubectl apply -f passing.yaml should succeed and Gatekeeper should record no violations.
- Validate that namespaces have the required NetworkPolicy objects and that deployments use trusted SAs with automountServiceAccountToken disabled.
